N-1.9-A.skill: evaluate a limit of a composite g(f(x)) by combining a verbally described graph of f with a piecewise rule for g, tracking the side from which f(x) approaches the inner limit.

N-1.9-B.skill: evaluate a one-sided limit of f(c − x) or f(c·x) from limits of f at a point, recognising that a negative inside factor swaps the side of approach.

N-1.10-A.skill: classify discontinuities of a rational function containing an absolute value by comparing one-sided limits, distinguishing jump from removable and infinite types.

N-1.10-B.skill: choose the parameter that turns a discontinuity at a break point into a removable one rather than a jump, using one-sided limits and a given point value.

N-1.11-A.skill: apply the three-part definition of continuity at two junctions of a three-piece function, writing and solving two linear equations for the middle piece's coefficients.

N-1.11-B.skill: find the parameter values that make a piecewise function continuous at a point when the matching condition is a quadratic equation in the parameter.

N-1.12-A.skill: decide on which closed interval a function with a radical or logarithm and a rational factor is continuous, checking the domain and the points where the denominator vanishes.

N-1.12-B.skill: use a verbal description of limits and values at specific points to decide on which interval a function is continuous, applying one-sided continuity at endpoints.

N-1.13-A.skill: find the value that removes a discontinuity of a complex fraction by combining the fractions, factoring and cancelling to find the limit.

N-1.13-B.skill: combine a given function value with continuity at a point to determine unknown coefficients in the numerator of a rational function, using that the numerator must vanish at the removed point.

N-1.14-A.skill: determine the parameter values for which a rational function has exactly one vertical asymptote, using that a numerator zero cancelling one denominator factor removes that asymptote.

N-1.14-B.skill: analyse the sign of each factor to decide whether the one-sided limits at two vertical asymptotes agree, distinguishing an even-power factor from an odd-power factor.

N-1.15-A.skill: find a horizontal asymptote of a difference of expressions that is infinity minus infinity by multiplying by the conjugate before taking the limit at infinity.

N-1.15-B.skill: find both horizontal asymptotes of a rational expression containing |x| by rewriting |x| as x for x > 0 and −x for x < 0 before comparing leading coefficients.

N-1.16-A.skill: use the Intermediate Value Theorem on a table of values of a continuous function to count the zeros guaranteed, including a table entry equal to zero and intervals with no sign change.

N-1.16-B.skill: decide for which interval the Intermediate Value Theorem, applied to the endpoint values of a polynomial, guarantees a zero, recognising that equal signs at the endpoints give no guarantee even when zeros exist.
